title: Predictive SLO Degradation Forecaster & Adaptive Paging Integration
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy on-call pages and preempt customer-visible SLO breaches by forecasting high-confidence SLO degradation 15–60 minutes ahead and integrating predictions with the paging policy. Scope covers: trace-based features, a lightweight online forecaster that runs in the metrics pipeline, dashboard surfaces for confidence/lead-time, and an adaptive paging policy that can suppress, escalate, or reroute pages based on prediction confidence and cost-tier rules.

Why now: Current burn-rate alerts react after error/latency is already rising. Teams keep tuning thresholds, which leads to oscillation and pager fatigue. A predictive layer will give runbooks and platform automation time to remediate transient and early-developing failures without waking the on-call for every spike.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change existing SLO definitions or replace long-term capacity planning tooling. It also doesn't include on-host remediation runbooks (those are follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria:
- A production-safe feature extractor that consumes trace spans and metrics and emits 1-, 5-, 15-, 30-, 60-minute forecast scores for SLO error rate and p95 latency for per-route and per-model scopes.
- A forecasting service or pipeline stage that computes a confidence score and a recommended paging action (suppress/escalate/reroute) and writes results to the alert decision topic.
- Integration with paging policy engine so high-confidence imminent breaches trigger early notify (and low-confidence triggers reduce pages).
- Dashboards in Console showing forecast horizon, confidence distribution, and retrospective accuracy (precision/recall) for the last 7 and 30 days.
- Documentation: runbook for responders, instrumentation guide for teams, and a short design doc linked from the ticket.

Key design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Model complexity: we evaluated ARIMA, Prophet, and a small LSTM. Chosen path: a hybrid two-stage approach — a lightweight statistical forecaster (exponential smoothing with seasonal components) in the fast path for per-route realtime decisions, and an offline ML model (gradient-boosted features over traces) for periodic calibration and anomaly scoring. This balances latency, interpretability, and operational cost.
- Data signal selection: using aggregated trace-derived signals (error ratio, tail-latency counts, sampler-adjusted span counts) to avoid heavy cardinality explosion. We add a deterministic low-rate span hook for error-context capture when a route's error rate crosses a threshold.
- Placement: forecast stage will be placed in the metrics pipeline (between Kafka and the metrics store) to allow decisions before metrics are fully rolled up in long-term storage. This reduces decision latency but requires careful backpressure handling.
- Pager policy interaction: instead of an absolute block, predictions annotate alerts with a confidence value and recommended action. Policies are rule-driven and allow on-call teams to opt-in per service/team.

Instrumentation & engineering tasks (high level):
1) Trace hook library changes: add a short-lived deterministic diagnostic span that records last-error-context and synthetic trace sampling flags. (ENG-49922)
2) Metrics pipeline stage: implement forecast worker that consumes enriched time-series topics, runs the statistical forecaster, emits decision events to alert-decision topic. (ENG-49923)
3) Pager policy integration: extend policy engine to accept decision events and map to paging actions with configurable mappings and cooldown windows. (ENG-49924)
4) Console: add Forecast panel, Confidence heatmap, and Accuracy dashboard widgets plus a backtester view for model owners. (ENG-49925)
5) Docs & runbooks: design doc, responder runbook, instrumentation guide, and onboarding checklist. (ENG-49926)

Work-in-progress notes and recent updates:
- 2026-03-02 (Marco Liu): Kicked off spike to validate feature extraction from traces. Local PoC shows 1-minute error-rate forecasts correlate with 15-minute realized burn events about 72% precision on sample service. Link to spike notebook: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/forecast-spike
- 2026-03-05 (Sofia Nguyen): Prototype statistical forecaster implemented in Python; integrated with a Kafka consumer for the per-route timeseries topic. CPU/proc profiling shows median latency 35ms per batch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/2573
- 2026-03-07 (SRE review - Priya Rao): Concern about pipeline backpressure when forecasts lag; suggested a reservoir-based sampling fallback and circuit-breaker for the forecast stage. Added to tasks.
- 2026-03-09 (Data Eng - Omar Torres): Confirmed we can use the existing timeseries topic schema but need an extra field for deterministic-sample flags. Proposed migration plan in doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Forecast-Design
- 2026-03-11 (Sofia Nguyen): Implemented basic policy mapping; added suppress-with-confidence and escalate-with-confidence actions. Deployed to staging with feature flag. Staging: dashboards available at https://console.staging.redwood.ai/dashboards/forecasting
- 2026-03-12 (Marco Liu): Ran a 48-hour backtest against three services. Results: 65–78% precision at 30-minute horizon for p95 latency, suppressed ~40% of low-impact pages while catching 86% of high-severity incidents prior to burn-rate alerts. Added retrospective analytics to acceptance criteria.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How should team-level policies balance cost of false-negative missed preemptive pages vs. cost of false-positive noise? (Need product guidance and default profiles).
- Define SLAs for the forecaster: acceptable latency to deliver a decision event (target < 10s at tail) and availability targets.
- Entitlement model for enabling predictive paging (hosted vs dedicated customers).

Next milestones (timeline):

- 2026-03-26: Deploy forecast worker to canary namespace and begin phased on-call opt-in (ENG-49923 + ENG-49924).
- 2026-04-02: Complete Console dashboards and runbook, evaluate metrics for GA decision.

QA & rollout plan:
- Start with internal services only (three teams) running with 'observe-only' mode for 2 weeks. Measure precision/recall and responder feedback.
- Enable 'auto-suppress' with low-confidence threshold for non-critical services.
- Expand opt-in to platform teams and monitor page-volume delta and MTTR impact.

Notes for reviewers:
- Check the Forecast worker's resource footprint assumptions in the design doc. We chose a per-partition scaling model; alternatives are warm workers per service.
- Review privacy implications of deterministic sampling for spans; ensure we only capture non-sensitive identifiers and respect PII redaction rules.
- Product: provide default policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) so teams can opt-in easily.
